title: Árpád
fact_summary: The Hungarian prince named in the Byzantine chapter, elected in Etelköz and driven out with his people by the Pechenegs. Later Hungarian tradition makes him the son of Álmos and ancestor of the kings.

claims.text: The chapter says the Khazar khagan offered Levedi the title of prince; Levedi declined and proposed voivode Álmos or his son instead.

sources.locator: summary of DAI ch. 38 (exact page not fixed in the copy read)

claims.certainty_reason: Read only as Tóth summarises and quotes the chapter in Hungarian.

claims.text: It says Árpád was then installed as prince in Etelköz by being raised on a shield.

sources.locator: summary of DAI ch. 38 (exact page not fixed in the copy read)

claims.certainty_reason: Read only as Tóth summarises and quotes the chapter in Hungarian.

claims.text: One passage says the Pechenegs fell upon the Turks and drove them out together with their prince, Árpád.
claims.certainty_reason: Read only as Tóth summarises and quotes the chapter in Hungarian.

claims.text: A 2022 genome study calls the 10th and 11th centuries the “early Árpádian Period”, after the ruling house.
claims.certainty_reason: This records what the study reports, read in the open copy linked under Sources.

claims.text: Using the two generations of leaders, Levedi and Árpád, the son of Álmos, the story told in chapter 38 belongs to the second half of the ninth century.
claims.certainty_reason: Argued by one tier B study.

claims.text: The Gesta Hungarorum, about 1200, calls Álmos the “father of Árpád” and has the seven leaders swear always to have a duke from the line of Álmos.
claims.certainty_reason: This records what the source says, read in Martyn Rady's English translation in the open copy linked under Sources. The Latin has not been compared.

claims.text: A 2021 genetic study gives his dates as “Árpád (845–907 AD)” and calls him “the Great Prince of the Hungarians who started the so-called Árpád Dynasty”. It also notes that the name of the dynasty was coined in the eighteenth century.
claims.certainty_reason: Stated in passing by a genetics paper. No source for the dates has been read, and they should be treated as traditional.

open_questions.text: Which source first makes Árpád the ancestor of the kings? The Gesta Hungarorum (about 1200) is the oldest read so far, three centuries after his time.
Where do the dates 845–907 come from? No source for them has been read.

review.note: Checked by Claude against open copies of every source. Marc spot-checks a sample.
